correctness.rationale: Every new forest face has shore shape (2,2),(2,3), or (3,2); this yields c3=t(p-1)(q-1)-C(t,2) and c4=C(t,2)(p+q-4). Projecting the signed relative degree-four differential to triple-supported tetrahedra decomposes it into unit-minor 2-edge blocks and rank-five primitive C6 incidence blocks. Each all-marked triple contributes the actual integral six-term 4-cycle, so kernel rank C(t,3), image primitive. A fixed deleted edge gives a Z-basis of the connecting image I_p tensor I_q, killing H2 integrally. The resulting free groups are H3 of rank (t-1)(p-1)(q-1)-(p+q-3)C(t,2)+C(t,3), H4 rank C(t,3); higher groups vanish. Simply connected plus free consecutive-degree homology supplies the full wedge equivalence. Standalone independent subset-based F2 computations passed all 65 parameter triples 2<=p<=q<=6 and the signed six-cell determinant check. Boundaries t=0,1 and p=q=t match known results; calculations are corroborative only.

value.rationale: The problem naturally asks how graph-fault size controls the topology of the vertex-induced forest complex of a dense bipartite graph. Prior known results cover the intact, first-defect and fully balanced-defect endpoints but do not determine the stages between them. The new theorem gives a complete two-shore, all-intermediate-size integral homotopy classification, including a genuinely nonmonotone S3-rank and the first S4 class exactly at the third matching deletion. These dimensions and primitive integer ranks encode structural topological phase transitions, not a routine renaming, isolated arbitrary invariant, or a small incremental numerical gain.
